about.heroQuote: HeightComparison started as a side project built around one simple observation: height numbers are almost useless without context. You need to see them. A 12 cm gap between two people at 165 cm is a genuinely different experience to the same 12 cm gap at 185 cm. The proportion changes. The visual relationship changes. Yet every other comparison tool on the internet just subtracts one number from another and calls it done.
whatItDoesParagraphs: The height comparison chart takes your measurements and renders them at true proportional scale. Every bar is mathematically sized relative to every other bar on the screen. No rounding, no visual shortcuts, no bars that look 'close enough.' If Person A is 170 cm and Person B is 198 cm, that 16.5% gap is visible exactly as it should be.

You can compare up to an unlimited number of subjects at once, which turns out to be useful more often than you'd expect. A family of five, a sports roster, a lineup of anime characters, a person standing next to a waterfall. All of it on one chart, all of it at scale.

The celebrity database covers athletes, actors, musicians, and public figures across regions including Bollywood, British, Asian, and American entertainment. The fictional character library pulls from official production guides and licensed databooks for anime, cartoons, DC, and fantasy franchises. These aren't crowd-estimated figures. They're sourced from the records that the creators and organizations themselves published.

There's also an image upload feature that slots a photo into the chart at real proportions, accurate to within 1 to 2 cm. Useful if you want to visualize yourself against a reference without manually measuring.

calculators.text: Compares a person's height and weight against WHO and CDC population data, with charts broken down by age and sex. It covers both adults and children.

calculators.text: Runs the Devine, Robinson, and Hamwi formulas side by side so you can see where each lands, rather than presenting a single number as if it's the whole answer.

calculators.title: Average Height by Country
calculators.text: Covers 46 countries with a sortable table, regional breakdowns, a world heatmap, and height extremes. It's the reference we kept wanting to have open in another tab when thinking about global height context.

calculators.title: Image to Height
calculators.text: Estimates height from a photo. There's also a morning height variation guide built into it, which matters more than most people realize when comparing measurements taken at different times of day.

about.noAccountTitle: No Account, No Payment, No Watermarks
noAccountParagraphs: This decision was made early and has not changed. The PNG export has no watermark. The celebrity database is not behind a paywall. There is no subscription tier that unlocks features. The full tool is free.

That's not a marketing angle. It's just how the tool was designed. Adding friction through account creation or paywalled exports would make the tool worse. Height comparison is not a premium activity.
accuracyParagraphs: Conflicting height records are common, particularly for celebrities. Where data conflicts, we normalize to the most recently verified figure from a credible public source, not the most widely repeated one. Character heights come from licensed official materials where possible. Landmark and object dimensions come from architectural and scientific reference sources.
about.footerQuote: Visualizing height context, one pixel at a time.

intro.title: Height Predictor and Adult Height Calculator - [ Height Calculator- Children Height Predictor ]
intro.description: Use this height calculator to estimate the future height of children, teenagers, and adults based on age, genetics, and growth patterns. It uses the Khamis-Roche method, which predicts adult height for ages 4 to 17.5 from age, height, weight and both parents' heights. In the original study, 9 in 10 predictions landed within 2.1 inches (5.3 cm) for boys and 1.7 inches (4.3 cm) for girls. For a child under 4, or a baby not yet born, use the parents-only calculator below.

khamisRocheCalculator.description: Instant height prediction using scientific growth models. Enter age, sex, height, weight and both parents' heights. Works for ages 4 to 17.5.

midParentalCalculator.description: Estimate predicted height using only parents' heights. Works for babies, very young children, and unborn babies too. If you are pregnant, enter both parents' heights to get your child's estimated adult height range. This uses the mid-parental formula, which usually lands within 4 inches (10 cm) of adult height.

howTallChild.title: How Tall Will My Child Be?
howTallChild.description: No tool can predict a child's future height with complete certainty. However, research on child growth patterns makes it possible to estimate adult height with reasonable accuracy.
howTallChild.factorsTitle: Modern height prediction calculators analyze three key factors:
howTallChild.geneticsText: inherited variants explain about 80% of height differences between people.
howTallChild.currentGrowthText: Age, height, and weight measurements refine the estimate.
howTallChild.statisticsText: Growth patterns observed across large populations by age and sex.
howTallChild.closing: The result is an estimated adult height range: a useful guideline, not a guarantee. Children's growth patterns are individual and can vary significantly based on health, nutrition, and timing of puberty.
howTallChild.sonTitle: How tall will my son be?
howTallChild.sonText: The Khamis-Roche calculator above estimates your son's adult height using his current age, height, weight, and both parents' heights. It gives a more personalized estimate than a formula based on parents' heights alone. Boys typically stop growing around age 18, though some may continue growing a little longer.
howTallChild.daughterTitle: How tall will my daughter be?
howTallChild.daughterText: The Khamis-Roche calculator above estimates your daughter's adult height using her current age, height, weight, and both parents' heights. It gives a more personalized estimate than a formula based on parents' heights alone. Most girls reach their adult height between ages 15 and 16.
howTallChild.babyTitle: How tall will my baby or toddler be?
howTallChild.babyText: For baby height predictor, use the mid parental height calculator above. It needs only the mother's and father's heights and gives a rough range. If you are pregnant, enter both parents' heights for an estimate before birth. A common rule of thumb doubles a boy's height at age 2, or a girl's height at 18 months, to estimate adult height.
howTallChild.workedExampleTitle: Worked example: predicting height from parents' heights
howTallChild.workedExampleIntro: A father who is 5'11" (180 cm) and a mother who is 5'5" (165 cm) add up to 136 inches (345 cm).
howTallChild.workedExampleDaughter: Daughter: (136 − 5) ÷ 2 = 65.5 inches, about 5'5.5". In metric, (345 − 13) ÷ 2 = 166 cm.
howTallChild.workedExampleRange: Expected range: about 4 inches either side, so roughly 5'6.5" to 6'2.5" for the son.
howTallChild.workedExampleClosing: For a child aged 4 or older, the Khamis-Roche calculator narrows that range because it also uses the child's current height and weight.
howTallChild.age2RuleTitle: Quick check for toddlers: the age-2 rule
howTallChild.age2RuleText: Double a boy's height at age 2, or a girl's height at 18 months, for a rough adult estimate. A boy who measures 34.5 inches (87.6 cm) on his second birthday points to about 69 inches (5'9", 175 cm) as an adult. Mayo Clinic lists this rule alongside the mid-parental formula.

teensAdults.title: How Tall Will I Be? Calculator for Teens & Adults
teensAdults.description: Teens asking "how tall will I be" can use the Khamis-Roche calculator. Enter your current age, height, weight, and your parents' heights for the most accurate estimate.
teensAdults.teensText: Growth plates are still open. The Khamis-Roche calculator gives the best estimate. Use current measurements for maximum accuracy.
teensAdults.teensItem2: Accuracy improves as you get closer to adult height
teensAdults.teensItem3: Most boys stop growing between 16 and 18; most girls by 14 or 15
teensAdults.adultsText: Growth plates close after puberty. For adults, height prediction is no longer relevant, but the Mid-Parental Height Formula can still estimate what height their children may reach.
teensAdults.adultsItem2: Use the Parent's Height tool to predict children's height
teensAdults.adultsItem3: Use the height converter for unit conversion
teensAdults.limitationText: No height calculator can account for medical conditions, growth hormone disorders, or premature puberty. If growth seems unusually fast or slow, consult a pediatrician.
teensAdults.noParentsTitle: What if you don't know your parents' heights?
teensAdults.noParentsP1: Both calculators on this page need both parents' heights, so neither can give a prediction without them. You can still track your growth: measure yourself every 6 months and check your percentile on a growth chart, which shows whether you are following your usual curve. If you are worried about your growth, a doctor can order a bone age X-ray, the most accurate prediction method.

ctaBanner.text: Ready to get your height prediction? The calculator is at the top of this page.

determinants.title: What Determines Height?
determinants.description: A child's final adult height is shaped by two factors: genetics and environment. Understanding both helps set realistic expectations for height prediction.
determinants.geneticsMiddle: of height differences between people (MedlinePlus). Tall parents tend to have tall children, though regression toward the mean applies — meaning very tall or short parents often have children closer to the
determinants.nutritionAfter: comes from environment. Growth hormone is primarily released during deep sleep.
determinants.timingText: Early puberty may produce a taller child temporarily but a shorter adult. Late puberty often results in a longer growth window and greater final height.

growthCharts.title: Average Height by Age (Growth Charts)
growthCharts.textAfterLink: track average height and weight from birth to young adulthood, covering boys and girls from ages 2 through 18. They show where a child falls on the height percentile chart relative to peers.
growthCharts.percentileAfter: represents the median height for that age and sex. Healthy children typically fall between the 3rd and 97th percentile.
growthCharts.expandText: To see how tall a child should be at a given age, read the 50th percentile line for their sex. If a child stays above or below the 3rd to 97th percentile range, talk to their pediatrician. For an exact percentile, use the height and weight percentile calculator.
growthCharts.note: Note: Pediatricians focus less on a single measurement and more on whether a child stays on a consistent growth curve over time.

boysGrowth.title: When Do Boys Stop Growing?
boysGrowth.p1Before: Boys usually experience their main growth spurt during
boysGrowth.p2: The typical growth timeline for boys looks like this:
boysGrowth.p3Before: During peak puberty, boys can grow 3-4 inches per year.
boysGrowth.p3Strong: Most boys stop growing between 16 and 18.
boysGrowth.p3After: Late developers may still add a little after that.

methods.title: Height Prediction Methods Explained
methods.subtitle: How to Predict Your Child's Height
methods.description: Researchers use several formulas to estimate adult height. Each method balances accuracy against the data it requires.

khamisRoche.title: Khamis-Roche Method
khamisRoche.p1: Considered the most accurate height prediction method that does not require bone age testing. Analyzes four inputs: child's age, height, weight, and average height of both parents.
khamisRoche.p2: Developed after studying thousands of children's growth patterns using linear regression analysis applied to population-level growth data. Because it includes current body measurements, it outperforms genetics-only formulas.
khamisRoche.item1Strong: ±2.1 inches for boys, ±1.7 inches for girls (9 in 10 predictions; half fall within about 0.9 in and 0.7 in)
khamisRoche.readyText: Have your child's age, height, weight, and parents' heights ready?

midParental.title: Mid parental height formula
midParental.p1: The child height predictor based on parents estimates a child's adult height using only the mother's and father's heights. This simple method works for children of any age, including babies and unborn children, but it does not account for the child's current growth.
midParental.formulaExplanation: The mid-parental formula averages both parents' heights, then adds or subtracts a fixed amount. For calculating child height by mid parental height formula, add the mother’s and father’s heights, add 13 cm for boys or subtract 13 cm for girls, then divide by two. For heights measured in inches, use 5 inches instead of 13 cm.
midParental.boysFormulaSub: The same result: the parents' average plus 2.5 in.
midParental.girlsFormulaSub: The same result: the parents' average minus 2.5 in.
midParental.exampleText: Example: A father who is 71 in (5'11") and a mother who is 65 in (5'5") give an estimate of 70.5 in (5'10.5") for a boy and 65.5 in (5'5.5") for a girl. In metric, a 180 cm father and a 165 cm mother give 179 cm for a boy and 166 cm for a girl.
midParental.exampleEstimateText: The estimate lands within 4 inches (10 cm) of final adult height. For the boy above, that is 66.5 to 74.5 inches.
midParental.item1: Works for babies and young children when no current growth data is available
midParental.item2: Typical accuracy: within ±4 inches (10 cm) of final adult height
midParental.item3: Does not account for current growth trajectory. Use Khamis-Roche for children over 4
midParental.item4: Can also be used as a rough baby height calculator or for unborn children
midParental.onlyHaveText: Only have parents' heights? Use the Mid-Parental Height Formula calculator above.
midParental.linkText: Scroll to top and calculate now
midParental.workedExamplePointer: See the worked example under "How Tall Will My Child Be?"

boneAge.title: Bone Age Method (Wrist X-Ray)
boneAge.p1: Doctors use X-rays of the left wrist to assess growth plate maturity. Growth plates are thin cartilage bands. Their thickness reveals how much growth remains.
boneAge.item2: Used only when doctors suspect growth disorders

bayleyPinneau.title: Bayley-Pinneau Method
bayleyPinneau.text: Combines bone age data with height-for-age tables. Calculates the percentage of adult height already achieved to determine remaining growth potential. Requires bone age testing.

rocheWainerThissen.title: Roche-Wainer-Thissen Method
rocheWainerThissen.text: Uses bone age, current height, weight, and parental heights. Improves accuracy in some cases over Khamis-Roche but requires clinical bone age measurement. Primarily used in medical settings.

age2Rule.title: Age-2 Doubling Rule
age2Rule.text: Doubles a boy's height at age 2, or a girl's height at 18 months. It needs no calculator and no parents' heights, but it ignores genetics, so treat it as a rough check for toddlers.

canIncrease.title: How can you increase height
canIncrease.description: Your genes largely decide how tall you'll be. But how well you eat, sleep, and stay active during childhood can make a real difference in whether you reach that potential.
canIncrease.nutritionText: Adequate nutrition supports bone development. Key nutrients:
canIncrease.sleepText: Growth hormone peaks during deep sleep.
canIncrease.exerciseText: Supports bone strength and overall development. Running, jumping, and sports encourage healthy bone growth.
canIncrease.warningText: No exercise, supplement, or stretching program can increase height once growth plates close. Predictions are estimates. Genetics is the dominant factor.

accuracy.title: How accurate is this height calculator?
accuracy.description: This height calculator uses the Khamis-Roche growth model, trained on long-term studies of child growth data. Its margin of error is ±2.1 inches for boys and ±1.7 inches for girls.
accuracy.is100PercentText: No. Every height predictor returns a likely range, not an exact value. Khamis-Roche is the most accurate method that needs no bone age test. A wrist X-ray for bone age is more accurate, and doctors order it when they suspect a growth disorder.
accuracy.errorKhamis: ±2.1 in for boys, ±1.7 in for girls
accuracy.miss1: 9 in 10 predictions fall within 5.3 cm (2.1 in) of final adult height for boys and 4.3 cm (1.7 in) for girls
accuracy.miss2: The parents-only formula is less precise: usually within 10 cm (4 in)
accuracy.miss3: Correct parent height data is required for reliable output
accuracy.miss4: Early or late puberty can reduce prediction accuracy
accuracy.miss5: Not suitable for children with known growth disorders
accuracy.disclaimerText: This height calculator is for informational purposes only. It is not a substitute for professional medical advice. If you have concerns about your child's growth, consult a qualified pediatrician or endocrinologist.

faq.q: How tall will I be?
faq.a: Your adult height depends primarily on your parents' heights and your growth timing. Use the height calculator above. Enter your current age, height, weight, and your parents' heights to get a predicted height range based on the Khamis-Roche growth model. If you are already 18 or older, your growth plates have closed and your adult height is set.

faq.q: How tall will my son be?
faq.a: Enter your son's age, current height, weight, and both parents' heights into the Khamis-Roche calculator above. Most boys stop growing between 16 and 18. The Mid-Parental Height Formula can also give a rough estimate: (Father's height + Mother's height + 5 inches) ÷ 2.

faq.q: Is a height calculator accurate?
faq.a: The Khamis-Roche method (used in this calculator) is one of the most accurate non-clinical height predictors available. In the original study, 9 in 10 predictions fell within 2.1 inches for boys and 1.7 inches for girls. Accuracy improves when the child is older than 4, measurements are precise, and parent heights are correct. Results are always a range, not a guaranteed value.

faq.q: Is any height predictor 100% accurate?
faq.a: No. Every height predictor gives a likely range, because genes, puberty timing and health all shift the outcome. Khamis-Roche is the most accurate method without an X-ray, with 9 in 10 predictions within 2.1 inches for boys and 1.7 inches for girls. A bone age X-ray is more accurate, and doctors order one when they suspect a growth disorder.

faq.q: Can parents' height predict my height?
faq.a: Yes. Inherited genes explain about 80% of height differences between people, and parents' heights are the best everyday measure of those genes. The Mid-Parental Height Formula provides a rough estimate using only this data. However, combining parent heights with the child's current measurements (age, height, weight) through the Khamis-Roche model produces significantly more accurate results.

faq.q: Can I predict my baby's height?
faq.a: For babies and infants, use the Mid-Parental Height Formula calculator above. It requires only the mother's and father's heights. This gives a rough estimated height range. Note that accuracy is lower for babies than for older children, since current growth data is not factored in. Once your child turns 2, the age-2 doubling rule gives a second quick check.

faq.q: How tall should my child be at their age?
faq.a: Use the growth chart section above to see the average height range by age for boys and girls. The 50th percentile represents the median height. Healthy children typically fall between the 3rd and 97th percentile. If your child is consistently above or below this range, discuss it with their pediatrician.

faq.q: What is the most accurate height prediction method?
faq.a: The most accurate method overall is bone age testing (wrist X-ray), used clinically by doctors. For non-clinical prediction, the Khamis-Roche method is the most accurate available. It uses age, height, weight, and parent heights, with 9 in 10 predictions within 2.1 inches for boys and 1.7 inches for girls. This is the method used in the calculator on this page.

meaning.title: What Does Height and Weight Percentile Mean?
meaning.p1Before: A growth percentile shows how one person's measurement compares to a reference group of the same age and sex. The
meaning.p1After: defines the 50th percentile as the median: exactly half the reference population falls above it and half falls below.
meaning.p2: Percentile does not mean percentage of a maximum. A child at the 90th percentile for height is taller than 90 out of 100 children of the same age and sex in the reference group. It says nothing about how tall they can grow.
meaning.referencePointsTitle: Two reference points that clarify the scale:
meaning.p50Value: = the average for that age and sex
meaning.p90Value: = taller than 90% of peers the same age
meaning.p3: A low result on the percentile height calculator does not mean something is wrong. A high result does not flag a problem. What matters is the pattern across multiple measurements over time, not a single number in isolation.

Infants gain several centimeters in a single month during this period, so small percentile shifts between visits are normal.
infants.p2: The infant height percentile calculator produces the most useful information when you run it across multiple well-baby visits rather than as a one-time check.

toddlers.p1After: reference data. Growth in this phase is steadier than in infancy but follows clear age-specific patterns. The child height percentile calculator accounts for age in months rather than years to keep results accurate for children who fall between birthdays.
toddlers.p2: Parents often run the height and weight percentile calculator for kids before annual checkups to understand what the numbers mean before meeting the pediatrician. The tool does not replace a clinical assessment.

boysGirls.title: Height Percentile Calculator for Boys and Girls
boysGirls.p1: Boys and girls follow separate growth curves, especially after age 8. Girls typically begin their growth spurt around ages 10 to 11. Boys tend to peak between ages 12 and 14. The height percentile girl calculator and the height percentile calculator for boys each reference sex-specific datasets from the CDC.
boysGirls.p2: Entering the correct sex is the single most important input for an accurate result. A girl measured against a male growth chart would show a meaningfully different percentile than her correct female result. The calculator applies the right curve automatically.

adults.title: Height Percentile Calculator for Adults

adults.p1After: . The height percentile calculator for adults is a straightforward population comparison: you are either taller or shorter than a given percentage of adults of the same sex.
adults.p2: The adult male height percentile calculator uses male-specific distributions because adult male and female height distributions are distinct. A result at the 50th percentile on the US adult male height percentile calculator corresponds to approximately 5 feet 9 inches (175 cm).

faq.q: What is a good height percentile?
faq.a: There is no single good percentile. The average range on a height percentile calculator runs from the 25th to the 75th percentile, and most people fall somewhere in this band. What matters more is whether your percentile stays consistent over time and fits your family's typical height pattern.

faq.q: How accurate is a height percentile calculator?
faq.a: A percentile height calculator is as accurate as the measurements you enter. The reference data behind the tool comes from large, nationally representative datasets from the CDC and WHO. Accuracy improves when you enter age in months rather than years for children, and when height is measured without shoes, standing straight for older children and lying flat for infants.

faq.q: Can adults calculate their height percentile?
faq.a: Yes. The adult height percentile calculator compares your height to a population distribution rather than a growth chart. The height percentile calculator for adults uses NHANES survey data to place your height within the distribution for people of the same sex. The height percentile calculator for men uses male-specific data, giving a precise comparison against the adult male population.

faq.q: Do boys and girls have different growth percentiles?
faq.a: Yes. The height percentile girl calculator and the height percentile calculator for boys each use separate CDC reference curves because male and female growth patterns diverge after early childhood. Girls grow faster in early adolescence and boys catch up later. Entering the wrong sex produces a meaningfully inaccurate result.

faq.q: What is the difference between WHO and CDC growth charts?
faq.a: WHO Child Growth Standards cover ages 0 to 2 and are based on data from six countries, designed as an international reference for optimal growth. CDC growth charts cover ages 2 to 20 and are built from US population data, making them the standard reference for clinical use in the United States. This calculator uses WHO data for infants and CDC data from age 2 onward.

intro.title: Ideal Body Weight Calculator
intro.description: <ibw>Ideal Body Weight (IBW)</ibw> is an estimate of the weight range associated with good health for a given height and sex. This ideal body weight calculator applies three established clinical formulas: the <devine>Devine</devine>, <robinson>Robinson</robinson>, and <hamwi>Hamwi</hamwi> methods to produce a range rather than a single number. The tool works for men, women, and pediatric patients. Enter your height and sex to calculate ideal body weight instantly.
intro.disclaimer: (IBW is a clinical reference, not a body goal. Weight is one of many health markers. Always discuss weight-related health questions with a qualified clinician.)

howToCalculate.title: How to Calculate Ideal Body Weight
howToCalculate.p1: All three IBW formulas share the same logic. Start from a base weight at exactly 5 feet (152.4 cm) and add a fixed amount per inch of height above that. The formulas differ in their base weight and per-inch increment, which is why they produce slightly different outputs for the same person.
howToCalculate.p2: Ben J. Devine introduced his formula in 1974 to help clinicians estimate drug dosages based on height and weight. It became the most widely cited ideal body weight calculation formula in clinical practice.
howToCalculate.stepsTitle: This is how to calculate ideal body weight step by step using the Devine method:
howToCalculate.step1: Measure your height in feet and inches.
howToCalculate.step2: Subtract 5 feet to get the number of inches above the base height.
howToCalculate.step3: Multiply those inches by the formula's per-inch increment.
howToCalculate.step4: Add the result to the formula's base weight for your sex.
howToCalculate.p3: The calculator applies all three formulas at once. You get a range rather than a single number, which is a more accurate representation of what ideal body weight calculation can and cannot tell you.

formulas.title: Ideal Body Weight Calculation Formulas
formulas.description: The three formulas below cover most clinical use cases. Each one applies the ideal body weight calculation formula as a linear function of height above 5 feet. All were originally derived in kilograms.

devine.title: Devine Formula
devine.p1: Ben J. Devine published his formula in 1974. It became the most widely cited IBW formula in clinical practice. The per-inch increment is identical for men and women at 2.3 kg, but the base weights differ by sex.
devine.maleFormula: 50 kg + 2.3 kg per inch above 5 ft
devine.femaleFormula: 45.5 kg + 2.3 kg per inch above 5 ft

robinson.title: Robinson Formula
robinson.p1: The Robinson Formula was published in 1983 as a refinement of the Devine equation. It raises the male base weight to 52 kg and lowers the per-inch increment to 1.9 kg, producing a leaner estimate for taller men. The female base rises to 49 kg with a 1.7 kg increment. Robinson tends to give the lowest IBW of the three formulas for tall individuals.
robinson.maleFormula: 52 kg + 1.9 kg per inch above 5 ft
robinson.femaleFormula: 49 kg + 1.7 kg per inch above 5 ft

hamwi.title: Hamwi Formula
hamwi.p1: The Hamwi Formula is the oldest of the three, published in 1964. It uses a higher per-inch increment for men and tends to produce the largest IBW estimates for taller individuals. It remains common in dietetic and clinical nutrition practice.
hamwi.maleFormula: 48 kg + 2.7 kg per inch above 5 ft
hamwi.femaleFormula: 45.5 kg + 2.2 kg per inch above 5 ft

women.title: Ideal Body Weight Calculator for Women
women.p1: The ideal weight calculator for women applies lower base weights than the male versions of the same formulas. This reflects two biological realities. Women carry a higher proportion of body fat relative to lean mass. Women also have lower average bone density and muscle mass than men of the same height.
women.p2: The Devine formula sets the female base at 45.5 kg against 50 kg for men. The Robinson formula raises the female base to 49 kg. The result is a lower IBW estimate at every height compared to the male calculation.
women.exampleTitle: Female IBW example at 5 ft 5 in (165 cm):
women.exampleRangeSummary: Healthy range across formulas: approximately 56 to 58 kg
women.p3: Factors including frame size, muscle mass from training, and hormonal variation all influence what a healthy weight looks like for any individual woman. None of the formulas account for these variables. The female ideal body weight calculator result is a reference band, not a target to reach.

men.title: Ideal Body Weight Calculator for Men
men.p1: The ideal body weight calculator for men produces higher estimates than the female version at every height. This reflects the greater average muscle mass and bone density in male bodies. Muscle weighs more than fat per unit volume, so a man and a woman at the same height can both be healthy while differing significantly in weight.
men.exampleTitle: Male IBW example at 5 ft 10 in (178 cm):
men.exampleRangeSummary: Healthy range across formulas: approximately 71 to 75 kg
men.p2: Highly trained men who lift weights regularly will often sit above their IBW while carrying low body fat. In these cases, IBW is a less useful clinical reference than direct body composition measurement. The male ideal body weight calculation gives a useful starting point but does not replace a full health assessment.

pediatrics.title: Ideal Body Weight Calculator for Pediatrics
pediatrics.p1: The adult IBW formulas do not apply to children. The ideal body weight calculator for pediatrics uses age- and height-based references instead, because children's bodies are still developing and their healthy weight range changes continuously as they grow.
pediatrics.p2Before: The most common method for ideal body weight calculation in pediatrics uses height to estimate expected weight based on growth charts. In clinical practice,
pediatrics.p2After: are the reference standards for pediatric growth assessment. A child's IBW is typically taken as the weight corresponding to the 50th percentile for their height on the appropriate growth chart.
pediatrics.p3: The calculator switches to this growth-chart method automatically when an age under 18 is entered. The result appears as a weight range rather than a single figure. For pediatric weight concerns, always work with a pediatrician. Growth tracking across multiple visits is more informative than any single measurement.

adjusted.title: Adjusted Ideal Body Weight Calculator
adjusted.p1: The adjusted ideal body weight calculator applies in clinical settings for patients whose actual weight is more than 30% above their IBW. At that point, using IBW alone for drug dosing underestimates metabolic activity, because some excess fat tissue is still metabolically active. Adjusted Body Weight corrects for this.
adjusted.exampleTitle: Worked example — actual weight 100 kg, Devine IBW 70 kg:
adjusted.p2: The 0.4 factor reflects the estimated metabolically active proportion of excess weight. Adjusted body weight is used most commonly in aminoglycoside antibiotic dosing, chemotherapy calculations, and renal dosing adjustments. It is not a weight target. It is a pharmacokinetic tool for clinical dosing decisions.

percentIbw.title: Percent Ideal Body Weight Calculation
percentIbw.p1: To calculate percent ideal body weight, divide your actual weight by your IBW and multiply by 100. This shows how your current weight compares to the estimate as a percentage.
percentIbw.p2: Percent IBW is used in clinical nutrition assessments to flag patients who need nutritional intervention. A percent ideal body weight below 70% is associated with significant nutritional depletion. Scores above 120% are used as one threshold in obesity-related dosing decisions.

healthyRange.title: Healthy Weight Range
healthyRange.p1: The healthy weight range sits around your IBW result, not at a single point. Because the three formulas produce slightly different figures for the same person, the spread between the lowest and highest result defines a practical healthy weight range. For most adults, this spread runs 3 to 5 kg across all three formulas.
healthyRange.illustrativeTitle: Illustrative range — male, 5 ft 9 in (175 cm):

vsBmi.title: Ideal Body Weight vs BMI
vsBmi.p1: Body Mass Index and Ideal Body Weight measure different things and answer different questions. BMI evaluates your weight category by dividing weight in kilograms by height in meters squared. It returns a category label: underweight, normal, overweight, or obese. Ideal body weight calculation, by contrast, gives an estimated weight to aim for rather than a category label.
vsBmi.row1WhatItDoes: Estimates a target weight based on height and sex
vsBmi.row1Limitation: Ignores body composition, frame size, and age
vsBmi.row2WhatItDoes: Classifies weight status using weight and height
vsBmi.row2Limitation: Same limitations, plus does not adjust for sex differences in body composition
vsBmi.p2: Neither metric accounts for how weight is distributed between muscle, fat, and bone. A person with high muscle mass can show a normal IBW and a high BMI. A person with low muscle mass can show a normal BMI and sit above their IBW. For a full picture, both are best used alongside body composition data from a clinician.

faq.q: What is the definition of ideal body weight?
faq.a: Ideal Body Weight (IBW) is a clinical estimate of the weight range associated with the lowest risk of chronic disease and best overall health outcomes for a given height and sex. It was originally developed to standardize drug dosing but is now used broadly in health and fitness contexts.

faq.q: How accurate are ideal body weight calculation formulas?
faq.a: They are useful statistical estimates but have significant limitations. IBW formulas do not distinguish between muscle mass and body fat. A highly muscular athlete might weigh more than their "ideal" weight while being extremely healthy. They should be used as one of many health indicators, not the final word on your health status.

faq.q: What is the difference between Devine, Robinson, and Hamwi formulas?
faq.a: The Devine formula is the most widely used in medical settings. Robinson developed a slightly leaner model specifically for taller individuals. Hamwi is a more traditional formula often used in nutrition counseling. Most people find the best result by looking at the average range produced by all three.

faq.q: Is ideal body weight calculation better than BMI?
faq.a: Neither is perfect. BMI gives you a category (underweight, normal, etc.), while IBW gives you a specific target weight. IBW is often more intuitive for individuals, but like BMI, it cannot account for body composition (muscle vs. fat ratio).

intro.title: Height Difference Calculator
intro.description: The Height Difference Calculator subtracts the shorter of two heights from the taller one and shows the gap in centimeters and inches. It also shows the percentage difference and names the taller person. Enter heights in cm or feet and inches. The calculator is free, needs no account, and updates as you type.

calculateSection.title: Calculate Height Difference
calculateSection.description: Enter a height for Person 1 and Person 2, then choose Metric (cm) or Imperial (ft/in). The difference in height calculator shows the gap, the percentage difference and the taller person below the inputs. It takes two heights at a time and works on any device. It uses the values you enter and does not adjust for shoes or posture.

howToCalculate.title: How to Calculate Height Difference
howToCalculate.p1: Height difference equals the taller height minus the shorter height. The difference in height calculator finds the taller person first, so the result is always a positive number. The order you enter the two heights does not change the answer.
howToCalculate.formulaText: Height Difference = Taller Height − Shorter Height
howToCalculate.p2: Feet and inches follow the same rule after one step. Convert both heights to inches, then subtract. 5'10" equals 70 inches and 5'3" equals 63 inches, so the height difference is 7 inches (17.8 cm).

percentage.title: Height Difference Percentage
percentage.p1: Percentage difference expresses the height gap as a share of the taller person's height. A raw gap in cm tells you the distance. The percentage tells you how large that distance is relative to the people involved.
percentage.p2: Person B is 8.3% shorter than Person A. The height difference calculator shows this figure next to the gap in cm. Both values update when either height changes.
percentage.p3: The base you divide by changes the number. This calculator divides by the taller height, so it reports how much shorter Person B is. To find how much taller Person A is, divide by the shorter height: 15 ÷ 165 × 100 = 9.1%. Both figures describe the same 15 cm gap.
percentage.p4: The same gap in cm becomes a smaller percentage as heights rise. A 10 cm gap equals 6.3% when the taller person is 160 cm and 5.3% when the taller person is 190 cm.

faq.q: What is a normal height difference between couples?
faq.a: No single gap is normal. In a study of 12,502 UK couples, the man was 14.1 cm (5.6 in) taller on average. Gaps of 10 to 20 cm covered about 42% of couples. The couple height difference calculator shows the gap for any two heights.

faq.q: How do you calculate height difference?
faq.a: Subtract the shorter height from the taller height: Height Difference = Taller Height − Shorter Height. For 180 cm and 165 cm, the difference is 15 cm. Divide 15 by 180 and multiply by 100 to get the percentage difference of 8.3%.

faq.q: Can a height difference calculator show percentage difference?
faq.a: Yes. This difference in height calculator shows the gap in cm or inches and the percentage difference. It divides the gap by the taller person's height and updates both values when either height changes.

faq.q: Is "percent taller" the same as "percent shorter"?
faq.a: No. Percent shorter divides the gap by the taller height. Percent taller divides it by the shorter height. For 180 cm and 165 cm, Person B is 8.3% shorter and Person A is 9.1% taller.

faq.q: What units can be used in a height difference calculator?
faq.a: This height difference calculator accepts centimeters and feet and inches. Switching units converts both inputs and the result at once.

shortestCountries.title: Shortest Countries in the World
shortestCountries.captionMen: Timor-Leste men average 159.8 cm, the shortest male average of any tracked nation. Six of the ten shortest countries for men are in South or Southeast Asia.
shortestCountries.captionWomen: Guatemalan and Filipino women average around 149 cm, the lowest female averages in the Americas and Southeast Asia respectively.
shortestCountries.paragraph1: The shortest populations sit predominantly in South and Southeast Asia and Central America. Timor-Leste records the lowest combined average globally, followed closely by Guatemala and Laos.
shortestCountries.paragraph2: In Guatemala, chronic malnutrition affects nearly a third of children under five, directly stunting skeletal development. Bangladesh and Nepal face similar constraints: protein-scarce diets, limited healthcare access, and structural poverty that limits growth potential from birth.
shortestCountries.paragraph3: These figures are not genetic ceilings. They are largely markers of historical underdevelopment, reversible, as South Korea and China demonstrated across the 20th century.

tallestShortest.title: Tallest and Shortest Countries by Average Height
tallestShortest.chartTitleTallestVsShortest: 10 countries spanning the full global height range — male (blue) and female (teal)
tallestShortest.chartTitleTop10: Top 10 tallest nations — male vs female
tallestShortest.caption: Across all populations, men are taller than women by 12–15 cm. This gap holds consistent regardless of overall height level, it is nearly identical in the Netherlands and in Bangladesh.
tallestShortest.paragraph: Average height varies widely due to genetics, diet quality, childhood health, and economic development. Northern European populations consistently rank among the tallest, while some South Asian and Central American countries show shorter averages shaped by historical nutritional limitations.

averageMale.title: Average Male Height by Country
averageMale.paragraph1: The average height of a man worldwide is approximately 171 cm (5'7"). This figure masks a wide spread, from Dutch men at 183.8 cm down to Timor-Leste at 159.8 cm. Northern and Eastern European men are the tallest group globally, averaging 178 to 184 cm. North Americans and Australians sit in the 176 to 179 cm band.
averageMale.paragraph2: Japan at 170.8 cm sits noticeably shorter than South Korea at 175.5 cm: a gap that has widened as South Korean diets and healthcare improved faster following the 1960s economic boom. Iran at 175.6 cm sits mid-table. India at 166.5 cm and Bangladesh at 163 cm sit at the lower end of the Asian cohort. Guatemala at 163.4 cm and Timor-Leste at 159.8 cm reflect the most severe documented nutritional constraints on record.

averageFemale.title: Average Female Height by Country
averageFemale.paragraph1: The average height of a woman worldwide is approximately 159 cm (5'3"). Netherlands and Montenegrin women, averaging 170.4 cm and 170.0 cm respectively, are the tallest female populations on record. Russia at 164.5 cm consistently appears in global lists alongside Eastern European countries that make up most of the top ten.
averageFemale.paragraph2: South Korean women at 163.2 cm stand notably taller than Japanese women at 158.0 cm, a gap that has grown over the past half-century. Filipino women average 149.6 cm and Guatemalan women 149.4 cm, the lowest verified female average in the Americas. The average height for women in Japan was around 148 cm in the 1950s and has since climbed by a full ten centimetres, one of the steepest documented rises for any female population.

maleAndFemale.title: Average Male and Female Height
maleAndFemale.callout: Across virtually every population, men are taller than women by 12 to 15 centimetres. This gap holds consistent across very different absolute height ranges, the difference in the Netherlands is roughly the same as in Bangladesh. It reflects hormonal differences during adolescence: testosterone drives a longer growth spurt in males, while earlier oestrogen onset in females closes growth plates sooner. The sex gap is not meaningfully affected by nutrition or economic development.

netherlands.name: Netherlands
netherlands.paragraph: Netherlands men have topped global rankings for decades. Dairy-rich diets and universal healthcare drive the result.

unitedKingdom.name: United Kingdom
unitedKingdom.paragraph: UK sits mid-table in Europe. Heights vary by region — northern England and Scotland tend to average slightly taller.

japan.name: Japan
japan.paragraph: Japanese heights have risen sharply since the 1950s. South Korean men at 175.5 cm have since overtaken their Japanese neighbours.

bangladesh.name: Bangladesh
bangladesh.paragraph: High rates of childhood malnutrition have historically limited growth. Urban populations show modest gains over recent decades.

iran.name: Iran
iran.paragraph: One of the fastest documented rises in the Middle East — average male height has increased an estimated 5 to 6 cm over 40 years.

canada.name: Canada
canada.paragraph: Canada's figures mirror Australia's closely, reflecting a well-nourished, high-income population profile. Growth has plateaued since the 1990s.

ireland.name: Ireland
ireland.paragraph: Ireland sits in the upper quarter of European rankings. Heights have risen steadily since the mid-20th century.

sriLanka.name: Sri Lanka
sriLanka.paragraph: Urban populations in Colombo show measurable height gains over two generations. Rural areas have lagged due to food insecurity.

southKorea.name: South Korea
southKorea.paragraph: One of the largest documented generational height increases ever recorded — men gained around 6 cm across two generations post-war.

india.name: India
india.paragraph: India's national average masks large regional variation. Men in Punjab average around 172 to 174 cm. Urban areas show consistent gains.

usa.name: USA
usa.paragraph: The US was once third tallest globally. It now sits around 47th for men, reflecting diet quality diverging from European peers after the 1970s.

denmark.name: Denmark
denmark.paragraph: Denmark consistently ranks in the global top five. Strong public healthcare and high dairy consumption from early childhood contribute.

chartForMen.title: Average Height Chart for Men
chartForMen.paragraph: The chart below shows how male height benchmarks stack up across major world regions, from Northern Europe at the top to Central America at the foot. Country-level data varies within each region.
chartForMen.caption: Regional figures are weighted averages. Individual countries within each region may sit above or below the band shown. Source: NCD-RisC and World Population Review.

globalAverage.title: Global Average Height
globalAverage.paragraph1: <who>The World Health Organization</who> and NCD Risk Factor Collaboration place the global average male height at approximately 171 cm and the global average female height at approximately 159 cm. These weighted figures pull lower than most Western country averages because they account for the large populations of South and Southeast Asia.
globalAverage.paragraph2: The global figure has been rising since the early 20th century, with the most dramatic gains in East Asia. South Korea and China gained around 5 to 8 cm per generation since the 1950s. Gains in Western Europe, which started earlier, have largely plateaued since the 1980s.

tallestMan.title: Tallest Man in the World
tallestMan.paragraph: Robert Wadlow of Alton, Illinois remains the tallest person in documented human history at 272 cm (8'11"). His pituitary gland produced unchecked growth hormone from birth, and his height had not yet peaked when he died in 1940 aged 22. The Guinness record for the tallest living man belongs to Turkey's Sultan Kösen at 251 cm (8'3"), whose pituitary tumour was treated surgically, halting further growth.

shortestMan.title: Shortest Man in the World
shortestMan.paragraph: Chandra Bahadur Dangi of Nepal, verified by Guinness World Records in 2012, was the shortest adult male ever documented at 54.6 cm (1'9"). He lived to 75, working as a farmer and craftsman. He was measured for the first time by Guinness when already in his seventies, remarkable given the health complications often associated with severe growth disorders.

tallestFemale.title: Tallest Female in the World
tallestFemale.paragraph: Zeng Jinlian of Hunan Province, China holds the record for the tallest woman in verified medical history at 246.3 cm (8'1"). Born in 1964, she grew rapidly due to pituitary gigantism and died at 17 in 1982. The current living record belongs to Turkey's Rumeysa Gelgi at 215.2 cm (7'1"), a web developer and disability advocate holding multiple Guinness titles.

shortestFemale.title: Shortest Female in the World
shortestFemale.paragraph: Jyoti Amge of Nagpur, India has held the Guinness World Record for the shortest living woman since 2011 at 62.8 cm (2'1"). Her condition is achondroplasia, the most common form of dwarfism. She is also a working Bollywood actress who appeared in the US television series American Horror Story.

distribution.paragraph1: Human height follows a normal distribution. When plotted across a large population, the data forms a near-perfect bell curve, most individuals fall close to the mean, with fewer people at either extreme. Roughly 68% of men fall within one standard deviation of the global mean, approximately 164 to 178 cm. The standard deviation for male height globally is approximately 7 cm. A man at 185 cm sits roughly two standard deviations above the global mean, taller than approximately 97.5% of the world's male population.
distribution.paragraph2: For women it is slightly smaller at around 6 cm.

whyDiffers.title: Why Average Height Differs by Country
whyDiffers.paragraph1: Height is shaped by both genetics and environment. Genetics sets the theoretical ceiling, tall parents tend to produce taller children but whether a child reaches that ceiling depends almost entirely on what happens during the first two decades of life.
whyDiffers.nutritionParagraph: <bold>Nutrition</bold> is the single strongest environmental determinant of adult height. Adequate protein and micronutrients during the first 1,000 days of life are critical to skeletal development. Dairy and meat availability in childhood consistently predicts national height rankings.
whyDiffers.healthcareParagraph: <bold>Healthcare access</bold> determines whether childhood illnesses divert energy away from growth. Countries with strong vaccination rates and low disease burdens consistently rank taller.
whyDiffers.economicParagraph: <bold>Economic development</bold> underpins both nutrition and healthcare. GDP per capita correlates strongly with average height because wealth enables better food, cleaner water, and medical care.
whyDiffers.calloutUS: The United States is the most telling case study: in 1914, American men ranked third tallest in the world. Today they sit around 47th globally, not because their genetics changed but because diet quality declined relative to European peers after the 1970s.

faq.q: What is the average height of men in the world?
faq.a: The global average height for adult men is approximately 171 cm (5'7"). This weighted figure draws from NCD Risk Factor Collaboration and WHO data. It is pulled lower by the large populations of South and Southeast Asia, where averages fall between 160 and 168 cm. Men in high-income European countries average significantly more, often 178 to 184 cm.

faq.q: What is an average height for a woman worldwide?
faq.a: The global average height for adult women is approximately 159 cm (5'3"). Netherlands and Montenegrin women average around 170 cm. Women in Guatemala and the Philippines average closer to 149 to 150 cm. Most women in Western countries fall between 162 and 168 cm.

faq.q: Which country has the tallest people?
faq.a: The Netherlands holds the top spot for both men and women in most recent datasets. Netherlands men average 183.8 cm (approximately 6'0") and Netherlands women average 170.4 cm (5'7"). Montenegro and Estonia follow closely. The Netherlands has held this position for several decades, attributed to dairy-rich diets, strong public health infrastructure, and genetic factors in the population.

faq.q: Has average human height been increasing over time?
faq.a: Yes, substantially. Average height has risen sharply over the past 150 years in almost every country, driven by improvements in nutrition, sanitation, vaccination, and healthcare. The most dramatic recent gains occurred in East Asia: South Korean men gained around 6 cm across two generations following rapid economic development. Gains in Western Europe have largely plateaued since the 1980s.

faq.q: What is the shortest country in the world by average height?
faq.a: Timor-Leste records the lowest combined average globally, with men averaging 159.8 cm and women 152.3 cm. Guatemala and Laos follow closely. These low averages reflect historical nutritional constraints and limited healthcare access rather than genetic limits on growth potential.
